overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of how a large language model is designed, pretrained, and shaped into an assistant. You'll be asked about attention, layers and parallel processing, the context window, pretraining data, compute, what a trained model retains, fine-tuning and human feedback, behavior guidelines, system instructions, and open-weight and closed models.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: A model processes the sentence "The nurse handed the patient her chart." What does attention do for the token "her"?

options.html: It swaps the token for the noun that sits closest to it
options.text: It swaps the token for the noun that sits closest to it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

options.html: It draws in information from the tokens most relevant to it
options.text: It draws in information from the tokens most relevant to it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Attention updates a token's representation with information from other tokens, taking more from the relevant ones.

options.html: It checks the token against a stored list of written grammar rules
options.text: It checks the token against a stored list of written grammar rules
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

options.html: It removes the token because pronouns carry no information
options.text: It removes the token because pronouns carry no information
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

forms.stemHtml: Why could transformers be trained on far more text than earlier designs in a reasonable time?

options.html: They need no chips, since they learn from rules instead
options.text: They need no chips, since they learn from rules instead
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

options.html: They skip most of the text and read only a small sample
options.text: They skip most of the text and read only a small sample
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

options.html: They process all tokens at once, so chips can share the work
options.text: They process all tokens at once, so chips can share the work
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Within a layer every token's update can be computed at the same time, so training can be spread across many chips.

options.html: They write all of a reply at once instead of one token at a time
options.text: They write all of a reply at once instead of one token at a time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

forms.stemHtml: You are partway through a conversation with a chatbot that has no memory feature. Which of these are in the model's context window as it writes its next reply? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Your earlier messages in this conversation
options.text: Your earlier messages in this conversation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The conversation so far goes in again with each new message, as long as it fits.

options.html: The model's own earlier replies in this conversation
options.text: The model's own earlier replies in this conversation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The model's replies are part of the conversation so far.

options.html: A conversation you had with it last month
options.text: A conversation you had with it last month
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the context window.

options.html: The web pages the model was trained on
options.text: The web pages the model was trained on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the context window.

forms.stemHtml: A model answers well in English and poorly in a language whose speakers publish little online. What best explains this?

options.html: Its tokens can represent English words and nothing else
options.text: Its tokens can represent English words and nothing else
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

options.html: Its corpus held far more English text
options.text: Its corpus held far more English text
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model's strengths follow the makeup of its pretraining corpus, and web-based corpora are mostly English.

options.html: Its context window is shorter for other languages
options.text: Its context window is shorter for other languages
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

options.html: Its developer wrote grammar rules for English only
options.text: Its developer wrote grammar rules for English only
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these is an example of inference?

options.html: Adjusting a model's parameters over months in a data center
options.text: Adjusting a model's parameters over months in a data center
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

options.html: Filtering a web crawl before a training run begins
options.text: Filtering a web crawl before a training run begins
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

options.html: Running a finished model to answer a user's message
options.text: Running a finished model to answer a user's message
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Inference is the running of a trained model to produce output. It happens every time the model is used.

options.html: Hiring contractors to write examples of good replies
options.text: Hiring contractors to write examples of good replies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about what a trained language model retains from its training text are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Most of the text is kept as patterns, with detail lost
options.text: Most of the text is kept as patterns, with detail lost
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Training compresses the text. What accumulates is whatever helps predict across many passages.

options.html: Some passages are kept word for word
options.text: Some passages are kept word for word
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Researchers have extracted word-for-word passages from a model's training text.

options.html: A complete copy of the text is stored for lookup
options.text: A complete copy of the text is stored for lookup
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a trained model retains.

options.html: Text published after training ended is added later
options.text: Text published after training ended is added later
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a trained model retains.

forms.stemHtml: A developer fine-tunes a base model on demonstrations that were all written to be brief and formal. What should the developer expect?

options.html: An assistant with broad new knowledge of formal subjects
options.text: An assistant with broad new knowledge of formal subjects
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

options.html: An assistant whose replies tend to be brief and formal
options.text: An assistant whose replies tend to be brief and formal
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The choices made by the people who write the demonstrations pass into the model's manner.

options.html: An assistant with a later knowledge cutoff than before
options.text: An assistant with a later knowledge cutoff than before
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

options.html: An assistant that continues text instead of answering
options.text: An assistant that continues text instead of answering
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

forms.stemHtml: What can a developer's published behavior guideline tell you about its model?

options.html: What the model will do in any given conversation
options.text: What the model will do in any given conversation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

options.html: What every business using the model has instructed
options.text: What every business using the model has instructed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

options.html: What the developer says it intends the model to do
options.text: What the developer says it intends the model to do
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! These documents state intent. The companies that publish them acknowledge that their models don't always match.

options.html: What text the developer used to pretrain the model
options.text: What text the developer used to pretrain the model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

forms.stemHtml: Two apps are built on the same model. One is playful and wide-ranging, and the other is formal and sticks to insurance questions. What most likely explains the difference?

options.html: Each app trained its own copy of the model from scratch
options.text: Each app trained its own copy of the model from scratch
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

options.html: Each app uses a different knowledge cutoff for the model
options.text: Each app uses a different knowledge cutoff for the model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

options.html: Each app splits the user's text into tokens differently
options.text: Each app splits the user's text into tokens differently
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

options.html: Each app places different instructions ahead of the chat
options.text: Each app places different instructions ahead of the chat
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! System instructions from the deploying business set an assistant's role, tone, and topics, while the model's parameters stay the same.

forms.stemHtml: A developer publishes a model's parameters for download. Which of these can someone who downloads them do? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Run the model on hardware they control
options.text: Run the model on hardware they control
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is local deployment, and nothing typed into the model has to leave those machines.

options.html: Train the model further on their own examples
options.text: Train the model further on their own examples
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The holder of the parameters can fine-tune the model, including training away its safety behavior.

options.html: Read the model's complete training text
options.text: Read the model's complete training text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on open-weight and closed models.

options.html: Require the developer to update their copy
options.text: Require the developer to update their copy
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on open-weight and closed models.

forms.stemHtml: What does an attention weight set?

options.html: How much one token takes from another token
options.text: How much one token takes from another token
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A high weight means a strong link and a lot of information transferred. A weight near zero means the other token is nearly ignored.

options.html: How many tokens the model can take in at one time
options.text: How many tokens the model can take in at one time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

options.html: How often the model picks a less likely next token
options.text: How often the model picks a less likely next token
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

options.html: How many layers a passage passes through in a model
options.text: How many layers a passage passes through in a model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

forms.stemHtml: An older language system reads a passage one word at a time, and each step uses the result of the step before. Its builders add more chips, and training barely speeds up. Why?

options.html: Each step has to wait for the one before it to finish
options.text: Each step has to wait for the one before it to finish
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A chain of steps in fixed order can't be split across chips. A transformer has no such chain within a layer, which is why added chips speed up its training.

options.html: Each chip can hold only one word of the passage at a time
options.text: Each chip can hold only one word of the passage at a time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

options.html: Each word has to be looked up in a dictionary on a single chip
options.text: Each word has to be looked up in a dictionary on a single chip
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

options.html: Each passage must be labeled by hand before chips can use it
options.text: Each passage must be labeled by hand before chips can use it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

forms.stemHtml: In a very long conversation, an assistant stops following an instruction you gave at the start. Which of these could explain it? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The instruction was dropped to make room for newer text
options.text: The instruction was dropped to make room for newer text
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is truncation. Text that no longer fits in the window is dropped or summarized, usually without notice.

options.html: The model's parameters changed during the conversation
options.text: The model's parameters changed during the conversation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the context window.

options.html: The instruction is now a few tokens among many thousands
options.text: The instruction is now a few tokens among many thousands
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Even when everything fits, an early instruction has to compete with a lot of later text.

options.html: The model was retrained on your later messages
options.text: The model was retrained on your later messages
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the context window.

forms.stemHtml: A model gives detailed answers about famous national events and thin, error-prone answers about one small town's history. What best explains this?

options.html: Its developer blocked questions about small towns
options.text: Its developer blocked questions about small towns
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

options.html: Its parameters are updated only for famous subjects
options.text: Its parameters are updated only for famous subjects
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

options.html: Its context window can't hold the names of small places
options.text: Its context window can't hold the names of small places
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

options.html: Its corpus held little text about the town
options.text: Its corpus held little text about the town
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Subjects that are thinly covered in the pretraining corpus are thinly covered in the model.

forms.stemHtml: A developer finished training its model a year ago. Its computing bill keeps growing as more people use the product. Which cost is growing?

options.html: Pretraining, which repeats for each new user
options.text: Pretraining, which repeats for each new user
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

options.html: Inference, which happens with every request
options.text: Inference, which happens with every request
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Training happens once per model. Inference happens each time the model is used, so its cost rises with the number of users and requests.

options.html: Data filtering, which is redone for every reply
options.text: Data filtering, which is redone for every reply
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

options.html: Tokenization of the original training collection
options.text: Tokenization of the original training collection
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

forms.stemHtml: Researchers prompted a model many times and recovered several hundred passages that matched its training text word for word, some of which had appeared in a single document. Which conclusions does this support? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The model consults its training text when it writes
options.text: The model consults its training text when it writes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a trained model retains.

options.html: Models can memorize some training passages
options.text: Models can memorize some training passages
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The passages came from the model's parameters, which shows that some text is retained exactly.

options.html: The model holds every document it was trained on
options.text: The model holds every document it was trained on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a trained model retains.

options.html: Even text seen once can sometimes be retained
options.text: Even text seen once can sometimes be retained
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The authors report that their method worked on passages found in just one document.

forms.stemHtml: During feedback-based training, raters consistently prefer replies that agree with the user. What is the model likely to learn?

options.html: To check each reply against a reference source
options.text: To check each reply against a reference source
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

options.html: To refuse any request that raters have not seen
options.text: To refuse any request that raters have not seen
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

options.html: To state its knowledge cutoff in every reply
options.text: To state its knowledge cutoff in every reply
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

options.html: To lean toward agreeing with what users say
options.text: To lean toward agreeing with what users say
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model trained to be preferred learns whatever earns preference, so the raters' tendencies become the model's.

forms.stemHtml: An article cites a company's published guidelines as proof that its chatbot never gives a certain kind of answer. What is wrong with that reasoning?

options.html: Guidelines apply only to models whose weights are published
options.text: Guidelines apply only to models whose weights are published
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

options.html: Guidelines state aims, and behavior has to be tested
options.text: Guidelines state aims, and behavior has to be tested
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A published document shows what a company says it's aiming for. Whether the model behaves that way can be established only by testing it.

options.html: Guidelines are written by the chatbot and can't be trusted
options.text: Guidelines are written by the chatbot and can't be trusted
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

options.html: Guidelines are kept secret from everyone outside the company
options.text: Guidelines are kept secret from everyone outside the company
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

forms.stemHtml: What do system instructions change?

options.html: The parameters the model acquired during training
options.text: The parameters the model acquired during training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

options.html: The text in front of the model as it writes
options.text: The text in front of the model as it writes
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! System instructions are text placed ahead of the conversation. They leave the parameters untouched, which is why one model can behave differently in different products.

options.html: The collection of text the model was pretrained on
options.text: The collection of text the model was pretrained on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

options.html: The number of layers that a passage goes through
options.text: The number of layers that a passage goes through
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements describe a closed model? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Anyone may download its parameters
options.text: Anyone may download its parameters
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on open-weight and closed models.

options.html: Its developer runs it on the developer's own computers
options.text: Its developer runs it on the developer's own computers
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The developer keeps the parameters and runs the model itself.

options.html: Its developer can update it or withdraw it
options.text: Its developer can update it or withdraw it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Because the developer holds the only copies, it keeps control over the model after release.

options.html: Its training code and data details are public
options.text: Its training code and data details are public
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on open-weight and closed models.

forms.stemHtml: Inside a trained model, "bank" in "she rowed to the bank" ends up represented differently from "bank" in "she paid the bank." What produces the difference?

options.html: A dictionary entry that the model looks up for each sense
options.text: A dictionary entry that the model looks up for each sense
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

options.html: A rule that engineers wrote for words with two meanings
options.text: A rule that engineers wrote for words with two meanings
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

options.html: A separate vocabulary entry for each meaning of the word
options.text: A separate vocabulary entry for each meaning of the word
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on attention.

options.html: Attention blending in information from the other words
options.text: Attention blending in information from the other words
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The token starts out the same in both sentences. Attention updates it with information from relevant tokens such as "rowed" or "paid."

forms.stemHtml: Which feature of the transformer let developers grow their models by adding hardware?

options.html: Its stored grammar rules, which replace most of the training
options.text: Its stored grammar rules, which replace most of the training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

options.html: Its small size, which lets it run on a single ordinary chip
options.text: Its small size, which lets it run on a single ordinary chip
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

options.html: Its habit of reading one word at a time in a strict order
options.text: Its habit of reading one word at a time in a strict order
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on layers and parallel processing.

options.html: Its parallel processing of every token within each layer
options.text: Its parallel processing of every token within each layer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Because each token's update within a layer is separate, the work can be divided among many chips, and more chips mean faster training.

forms.stemHtml: You ask an assistant about your employer's internal handbook, which has never been public, and you don't paste it in. Which statements are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The model can open the handbook on its own when asked
options.text: The model can open the handbook on its own when asked
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the context window.

options.html: The handbook's text is not in the context window
options.text: The handbook's text is not in the context window
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The window holds only the instructions, the conversation, and what you supply.

options.html: The handbook's text is stored in the model's parameters
options.text: The handbook's text is stored in the model's parameters
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the context window.

options.html: The model may still give a confident-sounding answer
options.text: The model may still give a confident-sounding answer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! With nothing in the window or the parameters to go on, the model can still produce a fluent answer built from general patterns.

forms.stemHtml: A model knows far more about the past twenty years than about the nineteenth century. What best explains this?

options.html: Its corpus held far more recent text
options.text: Its corpus held far more recent text
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The web holds much more text from recent decades, and a corpus built from the web inherits that imbalance.

options.html: Its knowledge cutoff removed older material
options.text: Its knowledge cutoff removed older material
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

options.html: Its training ran through the text in date order
options.text: Its training ran through the text in date order
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

options.html: Its developer chose to delete most older books
options.text: Its developer chose to delete most older books
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on pretraining data.

forms.stemHtml: What happens to a model's parameters while it answers users' messages?

options.html: They are adjusted slightly after each message a user sends
options.text: They are adjusted slightly after each message a user sends
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

options.html: They are replaced with fresh random values every day
options.text: They are replaced with fresh random values every day
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

options.html: They are updated from the web pages the model searches
options.text: They are updated from the web pages the model searches
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on compute and training runs.

options.html: They stay fixed, as they were when training ended
options.text: They stay fixed, as they were when training ended
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Answering messages is inference, which reads the parameters without changing them. Only training adjusts them.

forms.stemHtml: A model with no search tool is asked to summarize a famous novel and then to recite one particular page of it. Which statements are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It probably holds the plot in summary form
options.text: It probably holds the plot in summary form
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A widely discussed novel is well covered in training text, so its plot is retained as a pattern.

options.html: It retrieves the page from a stored copy of the book
options.text: It retrieves the page from a stored copy of the book
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a trained model retains.

options.html: It is unlikely to have most pages word for word
options.text: It is unlikely to have most pages word for word
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Most text is retained as patterns only. Exact wording survives mainly for passages repeated many times.

options.html: It holds the full text of every book in its corpus
options.text: It holds the full text of every book in its corpus
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what a trained model retains.

forms.stemHtml: Two developers start from similar base models. Each hires its own team, with its own instructions, to write example replies and rank outputs. What is the likeliest result?

options.html: Assistants that differ in manner and habits
options.text: Assistants that differ in manner and habits
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The people who supply examples and judgments, and the instructions they work to, shape how the finished assistant behaves.

options.html: Assistants that are alike in every respect
options.text: Assistants that are alike in every respect
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

options.html: Assistants that differ only in knowledge cutoff
options.text: Assistants that differ only in knowledge cutoff
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

options.html: Assistants that no longer follow instructions
options.text: Assistants that no longer follow instructions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fine-tuning and on training with human feedback.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these would be the best evidence of how a model in fact behaves on sensitive requests?

options.html: Results from testing the model on many such requests
options.text: Results from testing the model on many such requests
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Behavior is established by testing. Documents and self-descriptions show intent or produce plausible text, and neither shows what the model does.

options.html: The developer's published statement of the model's values
options.text: The developer's published statement of the model's values
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

options.html: The model's own description of how it handles them
options.text: The model's own description of how it handles them
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

options.html: A news report that summarizes the developer's guidelines
options.text: A news report that summarizes the developer's guidelines
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on published behavior guidelines.

forms.stemHtml: A travel company's assistant declines to talk about anything except travel. The same model, in a general-purpose app, discusses nearly any subject. Where does the travel assistant's limit most likely come from?

options.html: The travel company's system instructions
options.text: The travel company's system instructions
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A deploying business can narrow an assistant to a few topics through its system instructions.

options.html: The model's pretraining on travel websites
options.text: The model's pretraining on travel websites
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

options.html: The attention weights for the word "travel"
options.text: The attention weights for the word "travel"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

options.html: The size of the travel app's context window
options.text: The size of the travel app's context window
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on system instructions and safety training.

forms.stemHtml: A developer has published a model's weights, and many people have downloaded them. Which statements are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The developer cannot recall the copies
options.text: The developer cannot recall the copies
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Published parameters can't be recalled once released. Copies stay wherever they've been saved.

options.html: The developer can switch off every copy remotely
options.text: The developer can switch off every copy remotely
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on open-weight and closed models.

options.html: Holders can train away the model's safety behavior
options.text: Holders can train away the model's safety behavior
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Safeguards in an open-weight model are easier to remove, since the holder can train the model further.

options.html: The release counts as open source by definition
options.text: The release counts as open source by definition
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on open-weight and closed models.

title: Building a Modern Model
